headline: The shelf ran dry — and proved it
lede: Slot b took a refused TARGET, ran the ladder to its floor, and audited every title on the shelf with idle.mjs instead of manufacturing work: all six flagships are gap-free at c74273b, PINBALL's two open README gaps are one Jon-decision freeze (#3335, default keep-level-only) and one verbatim #3468 tail, and the last free score is GrindCity's #391 disclaimer. Every gap on every unheld title is owned — the legal dry stop, with tonight's throughput left to slot a (#3456 stage 2) and the two live QA lanes.

notes.text: #3456's claim lock is a stale ship-note, not a live claim: labels say game-queue (no building), but slot a's post-merge FORGE (a) comment (~05:20Z) reopened the 90-min window without release phrasing. Slot a's fresh session resumes it in its own namespace, so stage 2 still gets built tonight — no action, but ship-notes that reopen a queue item are read as holds (#3072).

Dry-shelf proof, computed not remembered: 72 registry titles, honest parseGaps over origin/main READMEs; flagship stage null; weakestStage PINBALL score 5 decomposes to 1 forbidden gap (#3335 AWAITING), 1 owned tail (#3468), 3 live-QA names; GrindCity's lone free bullet is a maintainer-chosen #391 disclaimer. The dry-shelf question itself is capped until ~Nov 27 — #2795's title ask was created Nov 20.

#3453 corpse status: rescue is in flight — qa/defender-seam-collision pushed (f05f16c), both QA sessions live; main checkout left byte-for-byte as found (step-1 detach refuses on the three files by design — a guard, not a failure). Slot b parked slot-scoped first (#1430), archived the halt-3436 report, reverted STATE.md, fetched to c74273b.
